Cold boot fails intermittently with LPDDR5X-7500. The bootloader reports DRAM training success but kernel panics 200ms into boot with random memory corruption.

Bootloader log:
  [pmic] VDD2H ramp to 1.05V: OK (sequence step 4/6)
  [pmic] VDDQ ramp to 0.5V: OK (sequence step 5/6)
  [dram] LPDDR5X DQS training: PASS (margin=18%)
  [dram] CA training: PASS (margin=22%)
  [dram] ZQ calibration done
  [boot] kernel handoff at 145ms
Kernel:
  [200ms] BUG: KASAN out-of-bounds at random addresses

The training margins look healthy. What in the LPDDR5X power-up sequence could complete training successfully but still cause random corruption shortly after? Consider VDD2H/VDDQ ordering, ZQ calibration timing, and RDQS strobe stability requirements at 7500 Mbps.
